status_note: RuleSubCommute generic tail commute loop order semantics (ticket BINSWEEP-SUBCOMMUTE-FREEVARNODE-0001, CR-SUBCOMMUTE finding 3): ruleaction.cc:4640 opSetInput(longform,newVn,i) must free vn from longform slot i BEFORE ruleaction.cc:4641 opSetInput(newsub,vn,0) attaches it, because Varnode::addDescend throws on a free varnode's second descendant (varnode.cc:334-336) and a still-read constant takes the Funcdata::opSetInput dedup copy (funcdata_op.cc:108-115) instead of the original identity. The reversed order was the P1 panic family on the ip corpus (3 functions, varnode.rs:2716) and a benign varnode-identity deviation for constants. Free varnodes are manufactured pipeline-style (COPY writer + opUnsetOutput -> makeFree keeps descend). 13 normal cases: free/free ADD (the panic form), free/const both orders, const/const, MULT/AND/OR16 free tails, single-input NEGATE, XOR at offset!=0, MULT free/const, same-written-vn dup-reuse leg (cc:4636 guard, cc:4646 reuse - exactly one new SUBPIECE), RuleSubZext overlap reject (cc:4623-4628, a pre-existing Rugra gap this fixture exposed and this ticket closes), second-reader reject (cc:4621). Trap mode (trap_dupfree, same free varnode in both XOR slots) locks the crash-form pair: the oracle itself throws LowlevelError rc=1 'Free varnode has multiple descendants' (0-byte stdout) vs Rugra panic rc=101 at varnode.rs:2716 with the same message - the varnode.cc:336 invariant is preserved on both sides, no golden. Coverage is ticket-domain scoped: the tail loop order + pre-check of RuleSubCommute::applyOp; the applyOp function-level status stays governed by the sibling tickets (RULEACTION-SUBCOMMUTE-SDIV-SEXT16-0001 residual UNTESTED plus ZEXT-PARTIAL/SUBZEXT-OVERLAP P3s).

decisive_semantics.reference_output_parameters: applyOp(op,data) mutates the IR by reference; the tail loop's opSetInput calls share live Varnode state across slots: opSetInput(longform,newVn,i) erases longform from vn's descend list (funcdata_op.cc:97 via opUnsetInput) BEFORE opSetInput(newsub,vn,0) calls vn->addDescend (funcdata_op.cc:123), so a free vn never observably holds two descendants; constants attached while still read would be replaced by a fresh copy inside opSetInput (funcdata_op.cc:108-115) - with the oracle order the slot is freed first so the original const identity survives (observable as keep=cn|readers=1).
decisive_semantics.loop_bounds_traversal_order: for i in 0..longform->numInput() (cc:4633), i!=j skips the INT_LEFT shift-amount slot; creation branch when lastIn != vn || newVn == 0 (cc:4636 - first slot always creates), reuse branch opSetInput(longform,newVn,i) otherwise (cc:4646); lastIn = vn unconditionally at each iteration tail (cc:4648); statement order inside the creation branch: newOp(2,subAddr) -> opSetOpcode(SUBPIECE) -> newUniqueOut(outvn size) -> opSetInput(longform,newVn,i) -> opSetInput(newsub,vn,0) -> newConstant(4,offset) inline at slot-1 time -> opInsertBefore(newsub,longform) (cc:4637-4643).
decisive_semantics.counter_accumulator_lens: lastIn and newVn are per-application locals initialized null before the loop (cc:4631-4632); newVn is rebound on every creation and reused by the dup leg; no cross-application state; the pre-check reads outvn->loneDescend() once (cc:4624) and compares the ZEXT output size against insize = base->getSize() read once at cc:4522.
decisive_semantics.sorting_comparison_keys: loneDescend identity is pointer equality (exactly one descendant else reject, cc:4621/4624); lastIn != vn is Varnode pointer identity (cc:4636); size comparisons numeric: ZEXT out size == insize (cc:4626), ext input sizes vs outvn size in the SDIV/SREM arms; keep-line readers observation uses pointer identity against the captured longform input varnodes.
